merger_description:
Kirin Holdings Company, Limited (**Kirin**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding share capital in Jamieson Wellness Inc. (**Jamieson**) (the **Acquisition**). Upon completion, Jamieson will transition to private ownership and will be solely controlled by Kirin.

Kirin is a company incorporated in Japan which engages in the manufacture and sale of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, pharmaceutical products, and natural health products worldwide through various global brands. In Australia, Kirin is primarily active in alcoholic beverages through its 100% ownership of LION PTY LTD, and in natural health products through its 100% ownership of Blackmores Ltd, an Australian manufacturer and distributor of vitamins and dietary supplements.

Jamieson is headquartered in Toronto, Canada and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Jamieson is active in the manufacturing and supply of vitamins and dietary supplements, including minerals, herbal remedies, probiotics, sports nutrition products, and over-the-counter remedies. It has global sales and its products are supplied in Australia under the brand names Jamieson and Youtheory.

Jamieson’s products are manufactured overseas for overseas markets. Jamieson’s primary business is concentrated in Canada, the United States, and China, but a small volume of its products is supplied into Australia through Jamieson’s global relationship with Costco.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, including one
or more of the parties’ revenues in Australia, the ACCC considers
that, if the Acquisition were put into effect, the notification
thresholds would be met.
The ACCC is unable to reach a view that the Acquisition would not be
likely to raise competition issues in any market based on the
information provided, given:
a. there is horizontal overlap between Kirin (through
Blackmores) and Jamieson in the supply of vitamins and
other dietary supplements in Australia
b. Blackmores is the leading provider of vitamins and other
dietary supplements in Australia
c. the relevant markets are unclear and the extent to which the
merged entity is likely to be constrained by alternative
suppliers is uncertain
d. the extent to which the Acquisition would remove any
competition from Jamieson or potential for expansion in
Australia is unclear.
The ACCC considers that the Acquisition warrants consideration
through the notification process, including via consultation with third
parties.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
